storm.summary_layperson: No thunderstorm activity is expected around the cove this evening — radar is clear, the atmosphere has almost no fuel for storms to form, and the next real chance isn't until Sunday night.
storm.local_effect_blurb: No storms are in play tonight, so the Sound's protective marine layer isn't being tested — instability is essentially zero (CAPE 30 J/kg).
storm.detail_html:
KOKX radar shows no storm cells anywhere in range this afternoon, and there are no active NWS alerts for the area. Instability is negligible — CAPE sits at just 30 J/kg, far below the threshold needed to support even weak thunderstorms, and the Sunday-Monday AFD discussion from OKX explicitly points the next chance of showers or storms to late Sunday night into Monday morning, not tonight.

Because there's no storm to weigh against, the local coastal-protection question is moot for the 17:00–22:00 window. The marine layer trend shows only a thin air–water buffer this evening (about 5°F now, thinning toward roughly 2°F by 7 PM as the air cools faster than the 75.6°F Sound water), but with nothing on radar to blunt, that number has no bearing on tonight's outcome.

Bottom line for the cove versus surrounding towns: everyone in the region should see a quiet, dry evening. There is no differential risk here worth flagging.

What would change this call: any new convective initiation appearing on KOKX radar, or an updated Storm Prediction Center outlook raising CAPE/shear support for the area before 22:00.

sea breeze collapsing, backing to light offshore gradient

wind.tactics_blurb: Sea breeze holds SSW through the first couple hours, softening as sunset (7:52 PM) approaches, then backs to a light NW/N gradient breeze for the back half of the window. Start mid-line, expect pressure to stay fairly even across the course, and don't count on more than 5-7 kt after sunset.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
This is a sea-breeze day, but a modest one — the air-water temperature difference (deltaT) is 5.0°F, right at the minimum threshold for the thermal to build, and only about half of coastal stations are showing the southerly sea-breeze signature (48% coastal-wide, though the western-LIS cluster closest to the cove is stronger at 70% southerly). RYC itself is reading S at 172°, 3 kt with a 6 kt gust — light but present and building. The background gradient wind is very weak (regional average speed 6.9 kt) and offshore, so it isn't fighting the sea breeze, just failing to reinforce it the way a true A+ tailwind day would.

There's a large divergence between HRRR and the actual station observations right now: the model already shows NW winds at 311° for this hour, while the real western-LIS obs are solidly S. This is a known HRRR failure mode where the model under-resolves the sea breeze early — since deltaT is below the 8°F gate used for the automated maturation correction, that correction didn't fire, so this forecast leans on observations and the geography/thermal pattern rather than raw HRRR direction for the pre-sunset hours.

Expect S-SSW flow through roughly 6-7 PM, fairly uniform across the course with maybe a touch more pressure toward the mouth and east shore, per the cove's geography. As deltaT crosses back below the 5°F sea-breeze threshold around 6-7 PM and sunset arrives at 7:52 PM, the thermal collapses — wind drops toward 5 kt and backs toward the light offshore NW/N gradient that HRRR has been forecasting (that signal becomes credible once treated as the post-collapse state rather than the current one).

Shift character: the first two hours should feel more persistent/oscillating within a fairly narrow SSW band (mature sea breeze, since local time is already past the ~15:00 ramp-up cutoff), then a real regime change as the thermal dies — racers should expect one clean transition rather than gradual oscillation late in the window. Wind for racing: 6-10 kt is a fine one-design window early; sub-5 kt after the collapse means the last race of a series is at real risk of getting light and shifty.

data_caveats: HRRR model data only extends to ~7:00 PM this cycle (8 forecast hours had fetch/parse warnings) — the 20:00-22:00 wind rows are extrapolated from the observed collapse pattern and gradient trend, not direct model output.

HRRR forecast wind direction diverges sharply from live station observations this hour (model NW 311°, obs S 185°, a 126° gap); the automated maturation correction didn't apply because deltaT (5.0°F) is below its 8°F trigger, so this forecast weighted live obs over raw HRRR for the pre-sunset hours.
